title: Limited English Proficiency in Healthcare: Federal Requirements
summary: Learn the federal language access requirements for patients with limited English proficiency, including Title VI, Section 1557, interpreters, translation, notices, and staff procedures.
body_markdown:
###


Title VI of the Civil Rights Act and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act are the main federal frameworks for language access in HHS-funded and covered healthcare programs.


###


Meaningful access means language barriers should not prevent an eligible person from obtaining, understanding, or participating in a covered health program or service.


###


No. HHS states that federal law does not require translation of every document. Organizations still need an appropriate written-language process for important patient communications.


###


No. Section 1557 does not prescribe one universal interpretation modality for every healthcare encounter. The language-assistance method must support meaningful access and meet the applicable qualification and communication requirements.


###


AI medical interpretation can be part of a language-access program when it provides usable spoken communication for the encounter and the organization has a clear path for unsupported languages, patient preference, accessibility needs, or unresolved communication.
